description:
New evidence is revealing important details about the origins of COVID-19 and challenging one of the biggest assumptions about how pandemics begin. Scientists have long believed that animal viruses need time to evolve before they can efficiently infect humans, but new research suggests some viruses may already carry the biological “key” they need from the moment they appear.

This video examines discoveries involving SARS-CoV-2, bat coronaviruses found in Laos, MERS, the 1918 Spanish Flu, and new research into how viruses cross the species barrier. Several wild viruses have shown an unexpected ability to bind directly to human cell receptors without first undergoing years of adaptation.
We also explore the role of ACE2 receptors, the furin cleavage site, interferon defenses, and why people in remote regions may be exposed to potentially dangerous animal viruses far more often than previously believed.
